findings.title: BackupCode component is named `TwoFactor`, which mismatches its file and the component it replaces
findings.description: The new file `BackupCode.tsx` declares `export default function TwoFactor({ center = true })`. The name is a copy-paste leftover from `TwoFactor.tsx`. Callers import it as `BackupCode` (`DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` and `login.tsx`), so the default import name is unaffected at runtime. In React DevTools, stack traces, and any future named import, however, it appears as `TwoFactor`, which is ambiguous next to the real `TwoFactor` component. Renaming the function to `BackupCode` would remove the confusion.

findings.title: Backup-code state is initialised with an untyped empty array
findings.description: `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);` infers `never[]`. The value is then written from `body.backupCodes`, which comes from an untyped `response.json()` result, and read through `.map(formatBackupCode)` and `key={code}`. The compiler accepts this, but nothing constrains the element type to `string`. Declaring `useState<string[]>([])` would make the contract explicit and let the compiler catch a wrong response shape.
